name: Pine64 (Pine Store Limited)
subcategory: community-oriented ARM/RISC-V single-board computers, laptops, phones and wearables
origin_detail: Founded in October 2015 in Fremont, California as Pine Microsystems Inc. by TL Lim (CEO, earlier behind PopBox and Popcorn Hour media players) and Johnson Jeng; launched with a December 2015 Kickstarter for the Pine A64 board that raised over $1.7M. Pine Store Limited was incorporated in Hong Kong in December 2019 and Pine Microsystems Inc. was dissolved in January 2020.
openness_notes: Hardware column. Pine64 sells low-cost hardware and relies on community-run, open-source software (mainline Linux and many PinePhone OS projects; InfiniTime on the PineTime; IronOS on the Pinecil), and describes letting 'FOSS principles guide our business'. For hardware it publishes schematic PDFs, component placement drawings, component lists and certification documents (e.g. PinePhone mainboard v1.1-v1.2b), but no PCB/Gerber layouts, and no open hardware licence is stated (only '(c) 2026 PINE64'). In July 2026 it released the full 3D file of the PinePhone and PinePhone Pro (licence not verified). Open software plus viewable but unlicensed, incomplete hardware documentation = level 2. Level at the first product (2016) was not verified.

license_history.license: Schematic PDFs and placement drawings published without an open hardware licence (PinePhone v1.1 'Braveheart' onward)
license_history.note: Year is the PinePhone Braveheart release (Feb 2020); publication date of the PDFs not verified. Footer copyright notice only; no CERN-OHL/CC licence found.

license_history.license: Full 3D file for PinePhone and PinePhone Pro released (licence not verified)

relicensing_events.to: Schematics plus full 3D (mechanical) files for PinePhone and PinePhone Pro
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Licence terms of the 3D release not verified.

risk_events: 2016: Pine A64 Kickstarter deliveries overshadowed by delays and shipping problems
2019-2020: corporate base moved from Fremont, California (Pine Microsystems Inc., dissolved Jan 2020) to Hong Kong (Pine Store Ltd); orders governed by Malaysian law as of late 2020
Ongoing: software support depends on volunteer community projects rather than the company
2026: PineTime revision needed to replace an end-of-life display part
robustness: Hardware is made and sold only by Pine64, but most software is community-maintained open source that would outlive the company, and published schematics help repair and porting. Small, low-margin business with no disclosed outside investment; still shipping new products in 2026 (PineVoice speaker, PineTime Pro samples).
physical_science_relevance: Low-cost ARM and RISC-V boards (Star64, Ox64) and the open-firmware Pinecil soldering iron are usable in lab automation, teaching and instrument prototyping.
openness_effect_assessment: Pine64 outsourced most software development to an open-source community (17 OS releases for the PinePhone per Wikipedia), which let a small company sell Linux phones, laptops and watches it could not have supported alone. Its hardware openness is partial (schematic PDFs, no layouts, no open licence), and the dependence on volunteers is also its main weakness. It remains operating and launching products in 2026 on Kickstarter-scale initial funding.
key_takeaway: Pine64 is the 'community supplies the software, company supplies cheap hardware' model: openness lives mostly in community-maintained software, while hardware is documented (schematics, now 3D files) but not openly licensed. Founded in California and moved to Hong Kong in 2019-2020, it has survived a decade on crowdfunding and sales rather than VC, at small scale.
